messages:
arjun: Quick thread — ambiguity on how we surface degraded routing/fallbacks to customers. Do we return a 200 with a quality flag, or a 503 with an 'explanation' so SDKs can trigger fallback logic? Example situation: model A overloaded -> route to cheaper model B with lower quality.

devon: I'm leaning 200 + explicit flag. mixing 200 + warnings keeps call semantics simple for clients that expect a body. propose header `X-Redwood-Degraded: true` + body field `quality_warning`.

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "quality_warning": "model_fallback_degraded",
  "data": { "choices": [ ... ] }
}
```

sasha: SDK note: many SDKs treat non-2xx as errors (throw). If we return 200, we need a clear SDK hook to emit telemetry and allow app authors to opt into stricter handling. header + telemetry event `degraded_response` seems necessary. Also we should surface a client-side boolean `responseIsDegraded` so apps can easily branch.

maria: Console UX: show amber badge per route when degraded rate > 3%. show sample degraded output in the rollout page and allow customers to toggle `strict_error_mode`. Also add an alert rule: `degraded_rate > 5%` -> page oncall. We should surface an event stream of degraded examples for customers to inspect.

chris: For hard failures (no content/timeout) use 503 + standard error shape + `Retry-After`. Also standardize `error_code` values: `fallback_partial` (returned content but lower quality) vs `fallback_none` (no content). Example 503 body:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "error_code": "fallback_none",
  "message": "Primary model unavailable; no fallback produced",
  "retry_after": 12
}
```

arjun: Backcompat concern: cannot bump major contract. propose we add `response_status` enum in body: `ok | degraded | failed` and keep 2xx/5xx semantics as-is. SDKs read `response_status` first, then header. That lets older clients still work (they see 200/500) and new clients can act on `response_status`.

devon: Also need billing clarity: degraded responses should be billable like normal in hosted product but flagged for quality-based credits on enterprise tiers. ops: tie to quotas/SLAs — e.g. a customer should be able to define whether degraded responses count against committed capacity.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to prod: inference-routing-v2 succeeded (3 hosts). :white_check_mark:

maria: I'll draft a short RFC with the schema, header names, SDK hooks, and console badges. assigning to @arjun @devon @sasha for contract draft. ack? :thumbsup:

arjun: ack

devon: ack

sasha: ack, will add telemetry event spec
